decisions: F1: Currency: the brief writes no amount with a currency sign or word, so position 'none' with empty symbol and word.

F1: Opening uses 'a digital assistant calling from <bank>' rather than <self> to follow 2.1's wording without repeating the bank name; not verbatim since the brief describes content, not an exact sentence.
F1: Callback window end 19:00 (Mail 2 correction replaces the 18:00 in Mail 1; this is an undated correction, not a dated amendment).

F1: Callback date rule: 'today or the next business day' read literally as include_today true with no business-day requirement on today (brief is silent), plus 1 business day ahead; windows apply on any allowed day.
F1: The 26 October 2026 holiday (memo OPS-26-118) affects callback dates via the shared calendar facet, not via this facet.

F1: banned.before_verification: the brief's three words plus product spoken names and generic purpose-revealing words, since the brief forbids naming the product before verification and the relative may not be told anything.
F1: right_party.reask equals the ask; brief says only 'Ask once more'. bare_no left to the default (third_party).
F1: reask_limit 1 per 3.3 ('ask once for another time'); vague_asks 1 and turn_budget 6 are generic defaults.
F1: No dated entries for this facet: the addendum's 14 October effective date changes notes/multi-product rules, not F1 values.
F2: Numeric-only dates read as DMY per 4.1 ('day, then month, then year').
F2: Phone question: length 4, pattern ^[0-9]{4}$, from 'last four digits' / 'four digits'.
F2: max_wrong per question 0: the brief only sets a total limit of three wrong answers 'whichever question they were on'.
F2: Hint day_month_swapped: counts_as_wrong false ('That retry does not count as a wrong answer'), max 1 since the brief gives no other number.
F2: max_declines 2: 'A second refusal or a second such question closes the call'; purpose questions count as declines.
F2: turn_budget and verified_prefix omitted (brief silent): generic defaults apply.
F2: All lines avoid 'collections', 'debt', 'payment' and product names, as 2.1 requires before verification.
F3: products.max = 1 in values because COL-P-07 v4 covers one product; the addendum A2 (effective 14 October 2026, 'one to three products') becomes a dated entry raising max to 3.

F3: The memo OPS-26-118 holiday (2026-10-26) has no separate effective date and names a single date, so it is added directly to calendar.holidays; the withdrawn 5 October draft (2 November) is ignored.
F3: Floors are product leaves: minimum_payment for credit_card, instalment_amount for personal_loan and car_loan; floor_missing = full.
F3: Statement intro paraphrases 5.2 ('calling from the collections team about a late payment'); item is one sentence per product per A2.2.
F3: count_from = after_today: 'the Nth business day after today' does not count today.
F3: numeric_order DMY from 4.1 and the DD/MM/YYYY holiday list; this_next current_week / following_week from 6.6.
F3: Band keys use the brief's names 'early' and 'late'; days ranges inclusive.
F4: promise_date.past_date omitted: the brief is silent on a past date beyond 'today or later'; the default applies.
F4: amounts.too_much.date = attempt_1: 7.3 does not tie the first floor offer to a specific date; only attempt 2 names the floor 'on the deadline'.
F4: The first ask is not a persuasion attempt (consumes_attempt false): 7.7 says a no to paying today is a flat refusal that then uses attempt 1.
F4: Ladder bands use the band keys 'early' and 'late' from the 6.2 table. Early has 1 rung (r1), late has 2 rungs (r1, r2), which matches the attempt counts 1 and 2.

F4: Attempt 2 offers the floor on the deadline even if the floor was already refused with the attempt-1 date. 7.3 allows this explicitly ('Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline'), so it counts as a different offer.

F4: The multi-product first ask comes from Addendum A2.4 (effective 14 October 2026). It was not added as a dated entry because it is only used for multi-product customers, which the addendum itself introduces. The multi_product facet holds that dating.
F4: above_full and decimals omitted: the brief is silent, so the defaults apply.
F4: forbidden_offers comes from 7.10 and the mail reminder 'Never quote a discount'.

F5: wants_human scoped id/neg/conf: the brief says 9.4 applies before and after verification, but transfer kinds never apply in rp/tp under the shared conventions; before the right party is confirmed nothing is transferred.
F5: Hardship precedence (800) is above restructuring (700) because 7.9 says it comes before 9.3; deceased/wrong_number are highest but scoped rp/tp only.
F5: Dispute precedence (550) is above already_paid (500) so that 'paid it off years ago' / 'closed' resolves as dispute per 9.2.
F5: Restructure transfer keeps recorded promises, drops unrecorded ones and suppresses notes per A2.10.
F5: Instalment-plan requests go to restructure_request (9.3 transfer); forbidden_offer covers discount/waiver requests (7.10, Mail 1).
F5: after_record set to ask_anything_else: the brief foresees a transfer after a recorded promise (10.1) and a request to change a recorded promise (8.3).
F5: Refuse-to-talk acknowledgement is a neutral 'I understand.'; dispute line avoids arguing; no pre-verification line contains banned words.
F6: recording.tries = 2: 'try once more' after a failed create_promise is one retry.
F6: Goodbye avoids <customer> because it is also said to third parties (relatives, wrong number) who are not the customer.
F6: Condolence sentence is a verbatim required sentence on S_DECEASED; 'ask nothing else' does not forbid the 10.3 thanks/goodbye, so S_DECEASED is not in no_goodbye.

F6: The 9.1 'payments can take one business day to appear' line is left to the paid intent's own say (it also fires per product in multi-product calls without closing), not duplicated in closing.per_situation.
F6: floor_offer adds 'The rest would stay overdue.' per 7.3; other lines keep generic defaults since the brief does not word them differently.
F6: The text-message sentence is said once (default once_after_all_creates) even with several promises.
F6: No dated entries: the addendum's multi-product read-back/recording rules only apply when several products exist and are expressed via readback/<items> and recorded_multi.
F7: Wire values taken from code list CL-COL-3 parts A-D (system values), never the internal codes; close_call.reason has no API enum so the code list's system values are used.
F7: Every situation's close reason comes from the result table in COL-P-07 10.1; PRM and PDA get reason '' because 'PRM and PDA take no reason.'
F7: S_REFUSED_TO_TALK maps to NOP / REF per 9.7 and gets note reason 'refused' (REF is in the A2.8 note-reason list). Refusing to talk before verification is S_ID_DECLINED (NVF / DCL).
F7: Transfer situations have note_reason '' because A2.10 says no notes on any transfer.
F7: notes.enabled is false in values (COL-P-07 10.2, policy as written). Addendum A2.8 turns it on from 2026-10-14 for every call, so that is a dated entry.

F7: Precedence: transfer_done -> transfer_situation comes first, as 10.1 says ('If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close with TRF') and A2.10 says (restructuring keeps earlier promises and closes TRF / RST). A2.13's 'PRM wins ... except under A2.10' is read as PRM beating no-promise products. It is not read as overriding 10.1's transfer rule, because A2.13 also says the 10.1 result table applies.
F7: Aggregation follows A2.13: all products PAID -> paid; otherwise NOP with the reason of the first product in API order whose situation is not PAID.
F7: unresolved_product_situation is S_REFUSED_EXHAUSTED (generic choice; the brief does not name one).

F7: multi_product values come straight from Addendum A2 and are not dated. Multi-product calls only exist under the addendum, which starts 2026-10-14. Before that, the standard covers one product only (1.1), so the multi-product keys have no effect.
F7: clamp_line keeps the generic wording. The brief only says to state the clamp in the read-back (A2.6) and gives no exact wording.
products.fields bound from the catalog: {"days_late": "days_late", "id": "product_id", "list": "products", "past_due": "past_due", "type": "type"}
interpretation.intent_tie derived from intent precedence: ['deceased', 'wrong_number', 'hardship', 'restructure_request', 'wants_human', 'dispute', 'already_paid', 'refuse_to_talk', 'too_much']
warnings: /intents/wants_human/keywords: '\\b(real|live) (person|human|agent)\\b' matches the intent's own negative 'Are you a real person?'

residual_rules.text: 2.3: If the customer asks a question during the right-party check, answer it first (2.4 robot/AI, 9.5 scam); the ask that follows is the second ask.
9.5 'Is this a scam?': say they can verify the call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, and continue.
9.7: a customer who says twice before verification that they do not want to talk is closed with NVF / DCL (S_ID_DECLINED).
API: an unreadable date_of_birth value is rejected with ok=false and is not counted as a wrong answer; ask again for the full date.

7.3: 'Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline' — repeating the floor amount with a new date (the deadline) is allowed even though the floor was refused before; no_repeat_refused_offer must compare amount and date together.
7.6: 'A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Handle it with section 6 and 7.1 to 7.4.'
A2.4: 'Do not ask about today again for each product. Start each product at attempt 1 of COL-P-07 7.7.' and A2.5 'Persuasion attempts are counted per product.'
6.6: '"Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week. "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week.'
9.6 A question the tools cannot answer: say you do not have that information. Do not invent figures, dates or reasons.
3.6 A relative may not answer the security questions and may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.
2.3 If the customer asks a question (robot/scam) during the who-is-on-the-line check, answer it first; the ask that follows is the second ask.
A2.12 A hardship mention covers every product that has no promise yet; if the customer declines support, each of those products is noted HRD.
A2.6: if one date named for everything is after one product's deadline, record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back.
8.4: say the promise is recorded only after create_promise returns ok: true.

A2.13: 'With several products, PRM wins whenever at least one promise was recorded, except under A2.10.' Taken literally, a human or support transfer after a recorded promise in a multi-product call could close as PRM. 10.1 says such a call closes TRF. The precedence rows cannot tell transfer types apart, so every transfer after a promise closes TRF.
A2.10: 'Promises agreed but not yet recorded are not recorded' when a restructuring request comes in. Agreed but unrecorded promises are dropped before the transfer.
A2.11: if one create_promise fails twice, keep the promises already recorded and note SVE for the failed product only. The call goes on with the other products.

sources./promise_date/latest: The **deadline** (latest promise date) depends on how late the customer is.
sources./promise_date/business_day_only: A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.

sources./promise_date/offered_date_refused: If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (7.7).
sources./promise_date/vague: If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day. If they still give none, propose the deadline.

sources./amounts/accept_max: If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it.

sources./negotiation/ladder/0:
Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
- Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
sources./negotiation/ladder/0/date: Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
sources./negotiation/ladder/1: Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.
sources./negotiation/ladder: | 1 to 7 | early | the 12th business day after today | 1 |

sources./negotiation/no_repeat_refused_offer: When the attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused.
sources./negotiation/non_answer_counts_as_refusa: A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt.
sources./negotiation/forbidden_offers: Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this standard.
sources./intents/0: 3.5 If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close with NRC / DEC.
sources./intents/1: 3.4 If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, close with NRC / WRN.
sources./intents/2: 7.9 If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Offer to connect them with the customer support team.
sources./intents/2/action/queue: If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue Q30 and close with TRF / SUP. If they decline, close with NOP / HRD.
sources./intents/3: 9.3 A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Call `transfer_to_agent` with queue Q10 and close with TRF / RST.
sources./intents/3/action: Promises recorded before the request stay. Promises agreed but not yet recorded are not recorded. Close with TRF / RST. On any transfer (restructuring, support or human) add no notes at all, before or after it.
sources./intents/4: 9.4 A request for a human: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue Q20 and close with TRF / HUM.
sources./intents/5: 9.2 "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product": do not argue and do not take a promise. Close with NOP / DSP. A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute.
sources./intents/6: 9.1 "I already paid": say that payments can take one business day to appear, take no promise, and close with PDA.
sources./intents/5/product_scoped: A2.9 A dispute (9.2) or an "already paid" claim (9.1) on one product does not end the call. Note it and continue with the others.
sources./intents/7: 9.7 If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close with NOP / REF. Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed with NVF / DCL.
sources./intents/8: A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in the same call. If the customer asks, say they can change it in the mobile app.
sources./intents/9: 7.10 Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this standard.
sources./intents/10: 7.3 If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once.

sources./outcomes/precedence/4: Otherwise close with NOP and the reason of the first product, in `get_account` order, whose note is not PDA.
sources./outcomes/reasonless_outcomes: PRM and PDA take no reason.
sources./notes/enabled: 10.2 Notes (`add_note`) are not used under this standard.
sources./notes/scope: For each product without a promise, call `add_note` with that `product_id` and a note reason (code list, part D)
sources./notes/skip_if_transfer: On any transfer (restructuring, support or human) add no notes at all, before or after it.
sources./multi_product/state_all_first: State every late product, one sentence each, before asking for anything.
sources./multi_product/ask_all_today_first: First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today.
sources./multi_product/order: go through the products one by one, in the order `get_account` returned them
sources./multi_product/attempts_per_product: Persuasion attempts are counted per product.
sources./multi_product/one_date_for_all: If the customer names one date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back.
sources./multi_product/clamp_line: record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back
sources./multi_product/readback_together: Read all promises back together and ask for one confirmation. Then call `create_promise` once per product.
sources./multi_product/hardship_applies_to: A mention of illness, a death in the family or job loss (COL-P-07 7.9) covers every product that has no promise yet.
sources./multi_product/dispute_or_paid_continues: A dispute (9.2) or an "already paid" claim (9.1) on one product does not end the call. Note it and continue with the others.

declared.name: customer_id
declared.meaning: Identifier of the customer, passed to every tool call.

declared.name: title
declared.meaning: The customer's title (Mr or Ms), used with the last name to address them.

declared.name: now
declared.meaning: The current date and time of the call, ISO YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM; every date rule uses it.

opening.line: Hello, I am a digital assistant calling from <bank>, and this call is recorded.

never_offer: any term that is not in this standard

answers.why: I'm sorry, I can only discuss that with <customer>.
answers.other: I'm sorry, I need to know who I am speaking with first.

third_party.reach_ask: When would be a good time to reach <customer>?
third_party.reach_reask: I can arrange a call back today or on the next business day, between 10:00 and 19:00. What time would suit?
third_party.outside_line: I'm sorry, I can't arrange a call back at that time.
third_party.vague_line: Could you tell me the exact day and time?
third_party.time_ask: What time on that day would suit, between 10:00 and 19:00?
third_party.booked_line: Thank you, we will call back on <date> at <time>.
third_party.offer_to_pay_line: Thank you, but I can only speak with <customer> about this.

questions.ask: For security, could you please tell me your date of birth?
questions.reask_wrong: I'm sorry, that does not match our records. Could you tell me your date of birth again?
questions.ask_full: Could you please give me your full date of birth, with the day, the month and the year?

questions.ask: Thank you. Could you please tell me the last four digits of the phone number we have on file for you?
questions.reask_wrong: I'm sorry, that does not match our records. Could you tell me the last four digits of your phone number on file again?
questions.ask_full: Could you please give me all four of the last four digits of your phone number on file?

hints.say: Could you say your date of birth again, with the month as a word?

decline.explain: These questions are there to protect your account.

identity.fail_line: I'm sorry, I was not able to verify your identity. Please use the mobile app or visit a branch.

statement.intro: I am calling from the collections team at <bank> about a late payment.
statement.item: Your <product> has a past-due amount of <past_due>, and it is <days_late> days late.

dated.source: A2.1 `get_account` returns one to three products.
It applies to every call from 14 October 2026, including a customer who is late on one product only: COL-P-07 10.2 no longer applies.

too_much.say_rest: The rest of the amount stays overdue.

below_floor.say: I'm sorry, <amount> is below the lowest amount I can record.

first_ask.single: Can you make this payment today?
first_ask.multi: Can you pay all of them today?

intents.label: Customer has died
intents.description: The person who answered says the customer has died.
examples: I'm afraid he passed away last month.
She died in the spring.
negatives: My uncle died last year, so money is tight.

action.say: I am sorry for your loss.

intents.label: Wrong number
intents.description: The person says the number does not belong to the customer.
examples: You've got the wrong number.
Nobody by that name lives here, this isn't his phone.

action.say: Thank you for letting me know, I apologise for the inconvenience.

intents.label: Hardship (illness, bereavement, job loss)
intents.description: The customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss as a reason they cannot pay.
examples: I lost my job two weeks ago.
My father passed away and I've been in hospital myself.
negatives: I can't afford the full amount this month.
keywords: \b(i was|i've been|i have been|i got|i've just been) (laid off|made redundant|fired|let go)\b
\b(i am|i'm|i have been|i've been) (\w+ )?(ill|sick|in hospital|in the hospital)\b

action.say: I am very sorry to hear that. Would you like me to connect you with our customer support team?
action.accept_say: I will connect you with our customer support team now.

intents.label: New payment plan or lower instalments
intents.description: The customer asks for a new payment plan or lower instalments.
examples: Can we set up a new payment plan?
I need lower instalments on this loan.
negatives: I plan to pay on Friday.

action.say: I will connect you with our restructuring team now.

intents.label: Asks for a human
intents.description: The customer asks to speak with a person instead of the assistant.
examples: I want to speak to a real person.
Put me through to a human, please.

action.question: Can I help you with that first?
action.say: I will connect you with a colleague now.

intents.label: Debt or product not mine
intents.description: The customer denies the debt or the product, or says the product was closed or paid off in the past.
examples: This debt is not mine.
I closed that card years ago.

action.say: I understand, I have noted that.

intents.label: Already paid
intents.description: The customer says they have already paid this past-due amount (completed, past tense).
examples: I already paid that.
I made the payment yesterday.
negatives: I will pay it on Friday.

action.say: Payments can take one business day to appear.

intents.label: Does not want to talk
intents.description: The customer says they do not want to talk.
examples: I don't want to talk about this.
Leave me alone, I'm not discussing it.
negatives: I don't want to pay today.

intents.label: Change a recorded promise
intents.description: The customer asks to change or cancel a promise that is already recorded.
examples: Can I change the promise I just made?
Actually, cancel that promise.
negatives: Can we change the date before you record it?

action.say: A recorded promise cannot be changed in this call, but you can change it in the mobile app.

intents.label: Asks for a discount or waiver
intents.description: The customer asks for a discount, a waiver or any term not in the standard.
examples: Can you give me a discount?
Could you waive the late fees?
negatives: Can I pay the minimum instead?

action.say: I am sorry, I cannot offer a discount or a waiver.

intents.label: Full amount too much
intents.description: The customer says the full past-due amount is too much or they cannot afford it.
examples: That's too much for me right now.
I can't afford the whole amount.
negatives: I can afford it, but not today.

intents.label: Asks if it is a robot or AI
intents.description: The caller asks whether they are talking to a robot or an AI.
examples: Am I talking to a robot?
Are you an AI?
negatives: I want to talk to a person.

intents.label: Asks if the call is a scam
intents.description: The caller asks whether the call is a scam.
examples: Is this a scam?
How do I know this isn't fraud?
negatives: Someone scammed me once, but go on.

action.say: You can verify this call by phoning <bank>'s customer service number.

confirmation.question: Do you confirm?
confirmation.what_to_change: What would you like to change?
confirmation.recorded_cannot_change: That promise is already recorded and can't be changed on this call, but you can change it in the mobile app.

recording.failed: I'm sorry, I could not record the promise.
recording.failed_item: I'm sorry, I could not record the promise for your <product>.

required_sentences.text: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.
I am sorry for your loss.

closing.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.

per_situation.S_ID_FAILED: For your security, please use the mobile app or visit a branch.

lines.floor_offer: I understand. Could you pay <floor> by <date>? The rest would stay overdue.
lines.clarify: Sorry, could you say that again?
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I don't have that information.
lines.date_ask_exact: Which exact day would work for you?
lines.next_bd_offer: That day is not a business day. Could you pay <amount> on <date> instead?
lines.deadline_offer: The latest date I can record is <deadline>. Could you pay <amount> by then?
lines.past_date: That date has already passed. Which day would work for you?
lines.above_full_offer: The amount due is <past_due>. Shall I record <past_due>?
lines.pay_on_date_question: Would you like to pay on <date>?
lines.cannot_offer: I'm afraid I can't offer that.
lines.account_error: I'm sorry, I can't access the account details right now.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?

multi_product.clamp_line: For your <product>, the latest date I can record is <deadline>, so I will use that date.
